body:
L’Dor Vador Travel Ltd.

Dated 18 October 2026  |  Version 1.2

Traveler agreement

These General Terms and Conditions govern travel packages and related services sold by L’Dor Vador Travel LTD, an Ohio single member limited liability company owned by its sole member, Hannah Berkeley Cohen, doing business as L’Dor Vador Travel or LDVD ("LDVD," "we," "us," or "our"). They explain how bookings are confirmed, what payments and cancellation charges apply, and the responsibilities of LDVD and each traveler. Please read them together with your Trip Schedule before paying.

Business street address: 90 Westwood Rd., Columbus, Ohio 43214, United States. Telephone: +1 614 382 2697. General inquiries: connect@ldorvadortravel.com. Reservations and cancellations: reservations@ldorvadortravel.com. Complaints: complaints@ldorvadortravel.com. Sole member and owner: Hannah Berkeley Cohen. This dated version applies when supplied and accepted for your booking; applicable registration disclosures are supplied separately where required.

1 Contract documents and scope

1.1 “Trip Schedule” means the dated trip description and booking disclosures supplied before payment, including the itinerary, inclusions, exclusions, total price, room basis, payment dates, cancellation terms, minimum group requirements, and any expressly incorporated supplier conditions. A booking confirmation records our acceptance of your reservation. “Departure” means the first scheduled service included in your booking at the destination, unless your Trip Schedule expressly identifies another starting point.

1.2 Mandatory law prevails over all contract documents. Subject to that rule, an expressly agreed written amendment prevails, followed by the Trip Schedule and then these Terms. A booking confirmation cannot introduce a new material restriction after payment without your agreement. Supplier conditions bind you only to the extent properly disclosed before the relevant purchase and legally applicable; they do not reduce LDVD’s own obligations.

1.3 These Terms cover consumer bookings with LDVD. Separate contracts govern any group organizer’s financial commitments and LDVD’s agreements with suppliers. A congregation, foundation, rabbi, group leader, or referring organization cannot change your contract or cancel your individual reservation without your authority.

2 Reservations and acceptance

2.1 Registering your interest is not a booking. A reservation becomes binding only when you have received the contract documents, accepted them, paid the required amount, and LDVD has issued written confirmation. A payment receipt or automated acknowledgment alone is not acceptance. If we cannot accept your reservation, we will return all amounts collected for it without a processing deduction.

2.2 The main booker must be at least 18 and legally able to contract. By making the booking, the main booker accepts these Terms and the Trip Schedule for themselves and all members of the booking party and represents that each adult party member has authorized them to do so. The main booker must give every party member a copy before acceptance, obtain the authority needed to provide their information and booking instructions, and communicate subsequent notices promptly. For a minor, acceptance and travel consent must come from a parent or legally authorized guardian, either directly or through the main booker with that guardian’s authority. A main booker’s acceptance does not waive another person’s nonwaivable rights or create authority that has not actually been granted. The Trip Schedule states any trip age restrictions.

2.3 Provide accurate passport names, contact information, and requested booking details, and promptly report errors in your confirmation. We will correct our own errors without an amendment fee. Any reasonable supplier cost caused by incorrect information you supplied will be disclosed before correction where practicable. We will not treat silence as consent to additional purchases.

3 Prices and included services

3.1 Prices are in U.S. dollars and per person on the room basis stated in the Trip Schedule. Only expressly listed services are included. The Trip Schedule must identify included hotel nights, room category, meals, transportation, guiding, admissions, and gratuities where included. Airfare, insurance, visas, personal expenses, optional activities, and pre or post stays are excluded unless expressly included.

3.2 We disclose the total mandatory price before payment. All mandatory charges are included in the disclosed total as required by law. Known applicable taxes and any unavoidable destination payments are identified before payment and included in that total where required. For an eligible credit-card payment, the amount and dollar value of any permitted surcharge under Section 4.3 are separately identified and included in the total shown before authorization. Optional purchases require your separate consent.

3.3 Once confirmed, your package price is fixed unless a specific lawful adjustment mechanism was prominently disclosed and accepted before booking. We will not impose a group size surcharge after confirmation without your agreement. If an obvious quotation error is discovered, we will explain it and offer you the choice of accepting the corrected offer or receiving a full refund, subject to any greater rights under applicable law.

4 Deposits and payment dates

4.1 Unless your Trip Schedule states otherwise, the proposed standard deposit is 25% of the package price per traveler, payable when booking, with the balance due 90 calendar days before departure. Bookings accepted within 90 days require full payment. Deposit payment is credited toward the price; its refundability is governed by Sections 6 through 9, rather than by the label “deposit.”

4.2 The Trip Schedule may require earlier payments for a particular hotel block, private event, flight, or other commitment, but those amounts and their cancellation terms must be disclosed before you commit. No undisclosed supplier obligation is passed through to you. You may owe a valid cancellation charge exceeding the deposit paid, subject to the agreed schedule and applicable law.

4.3 We accept the methods displayed at checkout or on the invoice. Stripe or another payment processor may process payment for LDVD; the processor is not the tour operator. Where permitted by applicable law, card-network rules, and our processor agreement, the total charge for an eligible credit-card payment includes a separately itemized 3% credit-card surcharge, calculated on the underlying amount paid by that credit card before the surcharge. The applicable rate, dollar amount, and complete payment total are shown before authorization and on the receipt. A card authorization is limited to the approved payment; installments or further charges require clear prior authorization.

4.4 If payment is overdue, we will notify you and allow five calendar days to cure, or a shorter reasonable period expressly disclosed where departure or a supplier deadline is imminent. If payment remains outstanding, we may cancel and apply the agreed traveler cancellation terms. Any retained sum or further amount sought remains subject to applicable law. Verify unusual payment instructions using a previously verified LDVD telephone number.

5 Minimum group size and departure status

5.1 Any minimum number of paying travelers and the date for deciding whether the trip will operate must appear in the Trip Schedule. If a minimum applies and no other decision date is stated, our decision deadline is 90 days before departure. Complimentary leaders do not count toward a paying traveler minimum unless expressly stated.

5.2 Before we confirm that the minimum has been met, your reservation may be identified as conditional. If the minimum is not met by the decision date, we may cancel and refund all package payments, operate at the agreed price, or offer a revised price or itinerary for your express acceptance. If you decline the revision, you receive a full refund. A substitute trip or credit is optional.

5.3 Once we confirm the minimum has been met and the departure will operate, subsequent reductions in attendance do not by themselves permit LDVD to cancel for low enrollment or raise your confirmed price. Other lawful cancellation grounds remain available. Do not buy nonrefundable independent flights until we confirm departure status in writing. “Guaranteed departure” does not guarantee against circumstances addressed in Section 9.

6 Cancellation by a traveler

6.1 Send reservation and cancellation notices to reservations@ldorvadortravel.com and include your name and booking reference. Cancellation takes effect when the message reaches our designated system, using the calendar date in Columbus, Ohio, regardless of acknowledgement. Contact us if acknowledgment has not arrived within two business days. The main booker or another authorized agent may cancel within the authority granted by the affected travelers. Notice to a group leader alone is insufficient unless that person is expressly authorized by LDVD to receive it.

6.2 Unless a different schedule was supplied and accepted before booking, the following standard charges apply to the canceled traveler’s package price. Each percentage includes the deposit and LDVD fees; it is not added to them. Separately disclosed, legally recoverable processing costs on a voluntary traveler cancellation are governed exclusively by Section 7.3 and are not charged twice. The percentage base excludes a separately itemized credit-card surcharge. Count calendar days backward from departure; departure day is day zero.

Notice received before departure: Cancellation charge

91 or more days: 10% of the package price

90 to 61 days: 25% of the package price

60 to 31 days: 50% of the package price

30 days or fewer, including no show: 100% of the package price

6.3 The schedule is intended to reflect reasonable expected booking, planning, and supplier losses, not to impose a penalty. It applies only to the extent permitted by law. We will account for savings, recovered sums, and resale where legally required and avoid double recovery. A separate item such as ticketed airfare follows different cancellation terms only if separately priced and disclosed before its purchase; it is excluded from the percentage base so the same item is not charged twice.

6.4 Illness, bereavement, inability to obtain documents, independent flight disruption, or a change of mind does not automatically waive a lawful traveler cancellation charge. Applicable legal rights and any insurance coverage remain available. If LDVD cancels or fails to provide contracted services, Sections 8, 9, and 23 apply instead; we do not characterize our cancellation as yours.

7 Changes and refunds

7.1 Requests to change names, dates, rooming, or travelers must be made in writing and are subject to availability and supplier approval. Before proceeding, we will quote any price difference and actual supplier amendment cost. These standard Terms impose no additional LDVD amendment fee. A change requiring cancellation and rebooking will be explained before you authorize it. An accepted replacement traveler may reduce cancellation losses where permitted.

7.2 We issue refunds to the original payment method where possible; if that is unavailable, we arrange a lawful alternative with the payer. Unless a shorter deadline applies, amounts owed by LDVD will be issued within 30 calendar days after entitlement and amount are established. We will explain disputed amounts promptly, issue undisputed sums on time, and not postpone a mandatory refund until suppliers reimburse us. Bank posting times are outside our control.

7.3 When you voluntarily cancel an otherwise available booking, you bear the actual, nonrecoverable payment-processing costs attributable to that cancellation, but only if their rate or calculation method and refund treatment were clearly disclosed before payment and the deduction is permitted by law and the applicable payment rules. The refund statement identifies any such deduction. No cost already recovered in a cancellation charge or retained fee is recovered again; no deduction may exceed the actual disclosed cost. LDVD bears processing costs when LDVD cancels, cannot accept or fulfill the booking, or owes a mandatory full refund, including where you decline a qualifying material change. Any credit-card surcharge is refunded in full or proportionately to the underlying amount refunded, as required by the card-network rules. We do not retain or relabel a refundable surcharge as a processing fee. Statutory airfare refunds under Section 11 remain controlling. Your bank may independently impose exchange or transaction charges. Credits and vouchers require your affirmative agreement and disclosure of their validity and restrictions; they do not replace a legally required money refund without your choice.

7.4 Voluntarily missed meals, activities, late arrivals, or early departures generally receive no refund to the extent services remained available and committed costs were incurred. This does not apply to services LDVD failed to provide or remedies required by law. Refund and dispute rights provided by your card issuer or law remain intact; duplicate recovery for the same loss is not permitted.

8 Changes or cancellation by LDVD

8.1 We may reasonably adjust timing, sequence, routing, guides, or similar operational details while maintaining the promised substance and standard. Where a contracted service is not delivered, mandatory substitution and refund rights still apply. We will notify you of known material changes promptly. A materially inferior hotel, significant loss of a principal heritage experience, or a substantial reduction in included services is not treated as a minor change.

8.2 For a material change before departure, we will explain available alternatives and offer you the choice of accepting the change, accepting an identified substitute, or canceling the affected booking for a refund of amounts paid for it. A lower value substitute carries an appropriate refund. We will state a reasonable response deadline, ordinarily at least seven days where timing permits. Silence is not acceptance of a material reduction; absent agreement we will cancel and refund the affected booking.

8.3 If LDVD cancels the entire trip before departure, we refund all amounts paid to LDVD for that trip. We do not deduct our planning costs, merchant fees, or supplier losses. You may elect an identified replacement or credit instead. Cancellation during travel or failure to provide individual services results in the applicable refund or substitution remedy for the undelivered services, with reasonable assistance arranging onward travel.

8.4 A named rabbi, host, or group leader may become unavailable. We will disclose that change promptly and seek a suitable replacement. If that person’s presence was expressly promised as an essential feature of your purchased trip, the material change procedure applies. We do not guarantee access to individuals or sites beyond what the Trip Schedule expressly promises.

8.5 Subject to mandatory law and LDVD’s liability for its own actionable conduct, we do not reimburse independent arrangements purchased outside your LDVD contract, such as separately booked airfare, parking, or visas. This restriction does not limit a refund or damages remedy that applicable law requires.

9 Events beyond reasonable control

9.1 Severe weather, natural disasters, epidemic restrictions, armed conflict, terrorism, civil disorder, government orders, border closures, and major infrastructure failure may prevent safe or lawful performance despite reasonable efforts. Financial difficulty, ordinary cost increases, insufficient enrollment, or a failure reasonably preventable by LDVD is not excused merely by calling it force majeure.

9.2 We will evaluate the actual effect on the trip, communicate reasonably available information, mitigate disruption, and provide the cancellation, refund, or substitution remedies in Section 8 and any mandatory law. This clause does not authorize retention of payments for an entirely canceled predeparture trip or waive obligations under Section 23. Supplier refusal to refund LDVD does not eliminate LDVD’s own refund duties.

9.3 If travel is interrupted, we will provide reasonable coordination assistance. Extra accommodation, transportation, medical care, or evacuation not included in your booking is ordinarily your expense unless LDVD is legally responsible or agrees otherwise. We will seek your authorization before discretionary extra expenditure where practicable. A government advisory alone does not necessarily cancel an operating trip; any mandatory legal cancellation right takes precedence.

10 Suppliers and local operations

10.1 LDVD assembles and sells travel arrangements and may contract with hotels, carriers, guides, museums, restaurants, local destination management companies, and other providers. Where engaged, a Curaçao LDVD company is a separate legal entity acting as a local service provider, not automatically your U.S. contracting party. The Trip Schedule identifies other package providers where required.

10.2 A provider may be independently owned or affiliated with LDVD. Its ownership, operational role, and the actual relationship govern; an affiliate is not described as independent merely because it has a separate registration. LDVD is not the operator of every vehicle, venue, or hotel. Subject to law, we are not automatically liable for a provider’s independent acts outside our control, but remain responsible for our own contractual obligations and any negligent selection, instruction, or supervision for which the law makes us liable.

10.3 Applicable carrier contracts and international conventions may govern transportation claims. No general reference to supplier terms eliminates LDVD’s refund, disclosure, or other mandatory obligations. Independently purchased optional excursions are separate contracts unless LDVD expressly sells or includes them.

11 Airline ticket sales and transfers

11.1 Scope and role. This section applies whenever LDVD sells or arranges scheduled airline tickets, whether alone, as an optional addition, or within a tour package. Airfare is included in a package only when expressly listed. LDVD acts as a ticket agent or reseller and does not operate aircraft. We may arrange issuance through an airline, accredited ticketing agency, host agency, or consolidator. Before payment we identify the contracting ticket seller, ticket issuer where different, and the entity collecting the airfare as merchant of record. Use of an intermediary does not remove LDVD’s own contractual or statutory duties. These Terms do not authorize public charter sales, which require separate compliant arrangements and documents.

11.2 Air booking disclosures. Before you authorize purchase, we provide an Air Booking Summary identifying the passenger, airports, travel dates, flight times, marketing and operating carriers, cabin and fare type, ticketing deadline, total price, baggage information, material restrictions, and LDVD service fees, if any. Flights operated under another airline’s code are identified as “Operated by” the actual carrier. Airline conditions of carriage and fare rules will be supplied or linked for review before purchase and apply only to the extent lawful. We disclose separate tickets, airport changes, overnight connections, or self transfer arrangements rather than presenting them as a protected through itinerary.

11.3 Price and ticket issuance. A quotation or reservation locator alone is not an issued ticket. Unless a binding fare hold or purchase protection applies, an unpaid quotation may change before purchase. We obtain your approval of the final itinerary and amount before issuing a ticket and do not charge a higher amount without authorization. Our air offers state the total mandatory price, including government taxes and required ticketing fees; optional services require affirmative consent. We do not increase the price of fully paid air transportation or a fully paid package containing it, apart from any government tax or fee exception lawfully available with the specific advance written consent required by law. These general Terms are not that consent. Any permitted increase after a deposit also requires the applicable specific prepayment disclosure and consent. Section 3.3 does not authorize a prohibited air price increase.

11.4 Payment and evidence of ticketing. Air purchases may require payment in full immediately, independently of a tour deposit. We disclose the ticketing deadline and any separate charges by the airline, LDVD, or issuer. We send the airline reservation reference and e-ticket number after issuance. Contact us promptly if they have not arrived by the promised time. If authorized funds are taken but a ticket cannot be issued on the approved terms, you may reject a replacement offer and receive a full refund of the unsuccessful air purchase. No airline accreditation or direct ticketing authority is represented unless verified and expressly identified.

11.5 Names and traveler information. Supply names matching the travel document to be used, together with date of birth and other legally required passenger data, and check the Air Booking Summary before approval. Name corrections and substitutions depend on carrier rules and may require reissue or a new ticket. Actual correction charges caused by incorrect traveler information will be disclosed before authorization where practicable. LDVD corrects its own booking errors without charging you an amendment fee. Entry and transit responsibilities remain as stated in Section 13.

11.6 Fare restrictions and voluntary cancellation. Basic economy, discounted, group, and consolidator fares may limit refunds, changes, seats, upgrades, mileage accrual, or transfers. The particular restrictions must be disclosed before purchase; a generic “nonrefundable” label does not replace those disclosures or eliminate statutory refunds. Voluntary changes may incur an applicable airline charge and fare difference. Before acting, we explain the available options and any quoted cost. Submit cancellation to LDVD under Section 6 and any urgent airline deadline stated in your Air Booking Summary. Contacting the airline may also be necessary during travel. We do not require LDVD acknowledgment as a condition of timely notice.

11.7 No automatic agency cooling off period. The federal airline requirement to offer a 24-hour hold or penalty free cancellation for qualifying advance bookings does not automatically apply to a ticket purchased through LDVD or another third party agent. We will identify any actual void window, hold, carrier benefit, or cancellation privilege available for your purchase before you pay. Do not assume that a ticket is refundable for 24 hours unless we expressly confirm that right. This paragraph does not limit any cancellation right separately required by applicable law.

11.8 Ticketing service fees. Any LDVD air service fee must be separately identified per traveler before purchase, with its amount, services, and refundability. No fee is charged merely because these Terms mention one. A fee described as nonrefundable may be retained only for an actual service beyond processing payment for a flight you found, with proper advance disclosure and only where law permits. We do not deduct merchant processing costs or impose an undisclosed refund fee from airfare we must return. Our own service failure, an unsuccessful ticket purchase, mandatory law, and any broader package refund promise remain controlling.

11.9 Airline cancellation or significant change. We promptly pass on material carrier notices received through our booking channels and explain available choices. For covered flights to, from, or within the United States, mandatory refund rights apply when the carrier cancels or significantly changes the itinerary and you decline the changed flight, alternative transportation, and compensation offered instead of a refund. Qualifying changes include departure at least three hours earlier or arrival at least three hours later for domestic itineraries, with a six-hour threshold for international itineraries; a change of origin or destination airport; added connections; a cabin downgrade; and qualifying disability related changes to connecting airports or aircraft accessibility. Applicable law determines the exact entitlement, including rights of accompanying travelers. An ordinary flight number change alone is assessed under the applicable rule and any effective government relief. For other routes, applicable local air passenger law and fare rules govern. Notify us of direct airline communications and monitor your carrier’s alerts. We do not accept a voucher or materially changed itinerary for you without authority.

11.10 Airfare refunds and the merchant of record. The Air Booking Summary identifies whether LDVD, the airline, or another disclosed ticket seller is the merchant of record, meaning the entity shown for the airfare transaction on your financial statement. If LDVD is responsible under 14 CFR 399.80(l), request the refund through us. We issue it within the applicable legal period: for credit card purchases, seven business days after the carrier provides the eligibility information specified in 14 CFR 260.6(d); for other payment methods, 20 calendar days after the refund becomes due. We promptly seek carrier eligibility information and do not delay a required refund pending return of airline funds. Other applicable automatic refund duties are honored. If another entity is responsible, we identify it and reasonably assist with the request; we do not substitute a referral for an obligation LDVD itself owes. The refund includes the legally refundable unused airfare, taxes, and applicable ancillary amounts, without duplicate recovery. Original payment is used unless you agree to a lawful cash equivalent. The general 30-day land refund period does not extend an air deadline.

11.11 Rebooking and credits. You may choose an available replacement flight or credit after being told of any money refund right. A credit is not imposed instead of a required refund. Where offered as an alternative to a mandatory U.S. cancellation or significant change refund, it must remain usable for at least five years and its material conditions and expiry must be disclosed. Credits arising from a traveler’s voluntary cancellation may have different disclosed fare restrictions. Accepting alternative travel may affect the right to a full fare refund; we explain that choice before obtaining your instruction. Fare differences for a voluntary change require approval. We do not waive other compensation, disability, or local law rights merely because you accept assistance.

11.12 Baggage and optional airline services. We supply the baggage notices and confirmation information required for your itinerary, including free allowances and applicable carry-on and first and second checked bag fees, through clear text or permitted specific links. Extra, oversized, or overweight baggage and optional services may cost more. Specific seats, meals, upgrades, and assistance are not guaranteed unless confirmed by the responsible provider. Notify us early of accessibility needs so we can coordinate with the carrier. Claims for lost, damaged, or significantly delayed baggage, baggage fee refunds, and unavailable airline ancillary services should be reported promptly to the airline within its lawful deadlines. The carrier ordinarily handles standalone baggage and ancillary service refunds; LDVD assists and honors any separate duty it owes. This does not reduce ancillary amounts included in a mandatory cancellation refund or other nonwaivable remedies.

11.13 Check in and connections. Observe airline check in, baggage, security, and boarding deadlines and use flight coupons in their required order. Missing a flight or deliberately skipping a segment may cause the airline to cancel later segments under disclosed fare rules. Separate tickets may require baggage collection, recheck, immigration, and a new check in; a missed connection may not be protected by the onward airline. We will identify such arrangements before purchase and use reasonable care in advising on connection times. Airline delays, denied boarding, rerouting, and carrier insolvency are addressed under applicable carrier obligations and passenger protection law. LDVD is not the operating carrier and does not guarantee airline performance, but remains liable for its own actionable errors and mandatory remedies.

11.14 Air tickets and the land package. An Air Booking Summary must state whether the air service is included in the package or sold as a separately priced addition, together with its interaction with tour cancellation. Air items with separately accepted cancellation rules are excluded from the land percentage cancellation base to avoid duplicate charges. Canceling land arrangements does not automatically cancel a separately contracted ticket; give us express instructions for each. Canceling or refunding air does not automatically cancel an otherwise operating land booking. These distinctions do not restrict package remedies under Sections 8, 9, and 23 where applicable, and a separately itemized price alone does not turn an included package flight into an independent contract. LDVD will not pass an included airfare loss to you contrary to its entire package cancellation refund promise. Unused airline value and recoveries are accounted for where required.

11.15 Transfers. The Trip Schedule specifies transfer eligibility, meeting points, and any arrival windows. Give us accurate flight details and report changes promptly. We will reasonably assist after delays, but a separately requested transfer outside the included arrangements may cost extra, with your consent. Missed independently booked flights do not automatically cancel an otherwise operating land package.

12 Accommodation and room sharing

12.1 The Trip Schedule identifies hotel nights, room category, occupancy, and any single supplement. Bedding, connecting rooms, early check in, late check out, and particular views are requests unless expressly confirmed. Hotel security deposits and incidental charges are your responsibility and will be disclosed when known. Substitutions remain subject to Section 8.

12.2 Roommate matching is an assistance service, not a guarantee. If a companion cancels or a match cannot be found, we will offer available room alternatives and disclose any single supplement before you accept it. We will not automatically charge an unaccepted supplement. If you instead cancel, the applicable traveler cancellation terms apply, subject to mandatory rights. A departing roommate’s cancellation charge must not duplicate a room loss already recovered from another traveler.

13 Travel documents and entry requirements

13.1 You are responsible for valid passports, visas, transit permissions, entry forms, parental consents, and other documents required for your citizenship and itinerary, including return or onward travel. Confirm requirements with official authorities. We provide general guidance and accurately communicate specific requirements known to us, but cannot guarantee admission by a government or carrier. Where denial is attributable to your failure to meet disclosed or official requirements, lawful traveler cancellation charges may apply; LDVD remains responsible for its own actionable errors.

13.2 U.S. citizens visiting Curaçao for a short tourist stay generally do not require a tourist visa. Each traveler, including a child, must carry a valid U.S. passport book for air travel, valid throughout the stay and with at least one blank page for stamps. Carry confirmed return or onward travel, accommodation details, and evidence of sufficient funds. Immigration determines admission and the permitted length of stay; travelers planning an extended stay, work, residence, or travel on another type of document must verify the applicable requirements separately.

13.3 Before departing for Curaçao, complete the mandatory Digital Immigration Card for each foreign visitor at the official portal, https://dicardcuracao.com/portal, within the seven days before departure. The official form is free. Keep its confirmation available digitally or printed for airline check in and immigration. A DI Card is not a visa or guarantee of entry. Confirm current requirements at https://www.curacao.com/en/article/what-do-i-need-to-visit-curacao and with the competent authorities before departure.

13.4 Yellow fever vaccination documentation may be required depending on travel from or transit through a risk country; it is not a routine requirement solely because a traveler is arriving from the continental United States. Where required, verify vaccination timing and any applicable exemption with official authorities and your healthcare provider. Arrange medical travel insurance covering treatment abroad, emergency care, and repatriation, as strongly recommended, and comply with any insurance or health requirement actually applicable at the time of travel. Transit countries and airlines may impose additional document requirements. Entry rules may change after booking; we will communicate material updates known to us.

14 Health and accessibility

14.1 Review the trip’s physical demands and seek advice from your healthcare provider when appropriate. Heritage itineraries may involve heat, stairs, uneven pavement, historic buildings, and extended walking. Tell us about functional assistance needs early so we can assess accommodations with you. Provide only information reasonably needed for safe service and accommodation.

14.2 We assess requests individually and comply with applicable disability and nondiscrimination law. Overseas facilities may have different accessibility features; we will seek accurate information rather than promise universal access. Tour staff do not ordinarily provide personal care, lifting, or continuous medical support. If such assistance is necessary beyond reasonable accommodations, discuss an appropriate support arrangement with us before booking.

14.3 Exclusion or removal for safety will be based on an individualized, reasonable assessment and lawful criteria, taking reasonable modifications into account. Disability, age, diagnosis, or a request for accommodation alone is not a ground for removal. Refund consequences depend on the circumstances, costs actually incurred, the contract, and applicable law.

15 Meals and religious observance

Tell us about allergies, dietary needs, and religious requirements before booking or as soon as known. A Jewish heritage itinerary does not by itself promise certified kosher food, Shabbat compliant transportation, prayer services, a minyan, or a particular standard of religious observance. Such commitments apply only when expressly confirmed. We will communicate accepted requirements to suppliers and exercise reasonable care; shared kitchens may create cross contact risks. Discuss serious allergies with us and your clinician. These provisions do not disclaim liability for LDVD’s own negligence or a supplier obligation we expressly undertook.

16 Conduct and group safety

Follow lawful local rules, reasonable safety instructions, and respectful standards at religious sites, cemeteries, museums, and private venues. Harassment, threats, violence, dangerous intoxication, or conduct creating a substantial safety risk may result in exclusion from an activity or the trip. We ordinarily give a warning and opportunity to correct behavior unless immediate action is reasonably necessary. We document the reason and offer reasonable assistance with onward arrangements. You are responsible for damage you cause and reasonable resulting costs to the extent legally attributable to you. We retain only lawful, supportable cancellation or unused service charges; removal is not an automatic forfeiture regardless of circumstances.

17 Travel insurance and emergencies

17.1 We strongly recommend insurance covering cancellation, interruption, medical treatment abroad, evacuation, repatriation, baggage, and relevant preexisting conditions. Insurance is mandatory only if the Trip Schedule expressly says so and identifies required coverage before booking. Coverage, exclusions, eligibility, purchase deadlines, and claims are determined by the insurer. We do not promise that a particular event will be insured. LDVD sells or advises on insurance only through legally authorized arrangements.

17.2 In an emergency we may contact your emergency contact and seek appropriate medical or evacuation assistance when you cannot consent, as permitted by law. We cannot guarantee local medical capacity or evacuation availability. You remain responsible for authorized or legally chargeable expenses unless another party is liable. Nothing here overrides an informed medical refusal, lawful advance directive, or LDVD’s duty to exercise reasonable care.

18 Risk acknowledgment

International travel involves risks including traffic, water activities, illness, crime, heat, and differing infrastructure and emergency services. Review official advisories, exercise reasonable care, and follow activity specific instructions. You may decline optional activities. You acknowledge ordinary inherent risks that cannot be removed through reasonable care. This acknowledgment does not release LDVD from liability for its own negligence, breach of contract, or other liability that the law does not allow it to exclude. Any activity specific release must be separately disclosed and legally valid.

19 Limits on liability

19.1 To the extent permitted by law, LDVD is not liable for indirect or consequential commercial losses, such as lost business revenue, arising from a booking. For ordinary economic loss claims arising from LDVD’s performance, LDVD’s aggregate contractual liability is limited to the package price paid or payable for the affected traveler.

19.2 Neither restriction applies to death or personal injury caused by negligence; gross negligence; reckless or intentional misconduct; fraud or misrepresentation; statutory damages, penalties, or attorney fees; mandatory refunds or restitution; or any liability or remedy that applicable law does not permit us to exclude or limit. These restrictions do not reduce a specifically promised refund or legally required supplier remedy. Nothing excludes responsibility merely because an affiliated company performs services.

20 Group leadership

20.1 A package may include tour leader travel, accommodation, or compensation and LDVD’s operating margin. No undisclosed extra payment is owed by travelers for these items. Any financial arrangements requiring separate disclosure will be identified before booking. A group organization’s separate contract does not authorize undisclosed changes to individual travelers’ rights.

20.2 The Trip Schedule identifies any promised group leaders and their roles. Leaders may assist with group communication, orientation, and educational or religious programming but are not automatically medical caregivers or authorized LDVD contracting agents. They may not change payment or cancellation terms, approve refunds, or receive cancellation notices for LDVD unless LDVD expressly authorizes them to do so. Changes in a named leader are governed by Section 8.4. The main booker’s authority for their own booking party is governed by Section 2.2.

21 Personal information and photographs

21.1 LDVD uses the information supplied for a booking to arrange and administer travel, communicate with the booking party, process payments and refunds, assess accommodation and safety needs, maintain transaction records, and meet legal duties. Relevant information may include names, contact details, passport and itinerary information, emergency contacts, payment references, and voluntarily disclosed dietary, health, or accessibility needs. Provide only information reasonably needed and obtain authority before submitting another person’s information. For questions about our handling of personal information, contact connect@ldorvadortravel.com  or use the business address and telephone stated above.

21.2 We share information needed for those purposes with relevant airlines, ticket issuers, hotels, transport operators, local destination management companies, other travel suppliers, payment processors, professional advisers, and authorities where legally required or otherwise lawfully justified.
